title: Scaled bar charts: read the scale, do not count lines
familyTitle: Reading a bar chart with a scale
skill: Read values from a bar chart whose scale steps by more than 1, then compare or add them.

concept: On a scaled bar chart one line on the side does not always stand for 1: the numbers on the scale say how much each line stands for.
Read the top of each bar against the scale, then add or subtract as the question asks.
explanation.visualNote: Reuses the family's own bars figure (with scale).

workedExamples.prompt: The bar chart shows mangoes sold at a shop. Read the scale carefully. How many mangoes were sold on Friday?
familyExplainSteps: The bar reaches 8 lines; each line is 50, so it shows 400

workedExamples.prompt: The bar chart shows mangoes sold at a shop. Read the scale carefully. How many more mangoes were sold on Friday than on Wednesday?
familyExplainSteps: The bar reaches 8 lines; each line is 5, so it shows 40
The bar reaches 1 lines; each line is 5, so it shows 5

hints: Look at the numbers on the side of the chart.

alternativeExplanation.title: Read the numbers on the side
text: Look at two numbers next to each other on the scale: their difference is what one line stands for.

whatWentWrong: In "The bar chart shows mangoes sold at a shop. Read the scale carefully. How many mangoes were sold on Thursday and on Friday together?", one wrong answer is 60.
Each line was taken as 10. Read the numbers on the scale: they tell how much each line stands for.
Do not assume 10: read the numbers on the scale to see what one line stands for.
